clauses.reason: Terminated by express revocation. EO 12553 of February 25, 1986 revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; the table lists 10283, whose subject line describes a board of inquiry to report on a labor dispute. No effective-date wording appears in the enacting provision, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (reading, disclosed for the reviewer); the exclusive and inclusive readings do not differ because this is not an until-date. Report deadline and status-quo period are not ends; functionally spent when the board reported and the statutory period ran, but the order remained on the books until this revocation (owner ruling 2026-10-21). No earlier express end was found.

research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10283 (16 FR 8873; govinfo PDF text layer of the official page, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10283 and signed August 30, 1951. The order creates a Board of Inquiry under section 206 of the Labor Management Relations Act, 1947 to inquire into the issues in a labor dispute affecting the copper and non-ferrous metals industry, with a report due on a stated date and a provision that, once the report is submitted, the Board continues in existence to perform other functions required under the Act until the President terminates it. Inventory: the order is one operative unit; the creation of the Board, its report date, and its continuation until terminated by the President are all within the single whole-order clause confirmed here. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held government printing) revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; its No. Subject table lists 10283 with a subject line matching this order (creating a board of inquiry to report on a labor dispute). The enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25; the Federal Register publication date 1986-03-03 and the filing date are not effective dates. The thirty-day or stated report date and the end of any statutory status-quo period are deadlines and spent facts, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines): the order stayed on the books until express revocation. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches (coverage notes read; no coverage warning) show no instrument other than EO 12553 revoking, superseding or amending this order; the held-text citation search found citations of this number only in printings of the order itself, orders printed on the same page, Federal Register index or codification-guide material and (for some) National Mediation Board report front matter.

savings.reason: The revocation has no savings clause and the order created no surviving appointment, transfer or right: bounded search of the held 12553 text, the order's own text and the OFR catalog shows no residual or continuing independent effect.
